opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__facts:
This second bail application in the shape of criminal appeal under Section 14A(1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, has been filed on behalf of the appellant seeking bail in FIR No.343/2022 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Vindhyanagar, District Singrauli, for the offence under Sections 376 and 342 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(V) of the SC/ST Act.
The appellant's first criminal appeal was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.09.2022 passed in Cr.A. No.7147 of 2022 granting liberty to revive the same after recording the statement of prosecutrix.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
He submits that after shouting by the prosecutrix, it is almost impossible that a person standing outside the room would not come for her help.
According to him, it was a case of consent and only after coming to know about the fact that the incident has been seen by some other person, then only the prosecutrix lodged a false complaint against the appellant.
He has further submitted that it is not a case of consent whereas it is a case of rape committed by the appellant.
He has submitted that looking to the nature of crime committed by the appellant, this appeal deserves dismissal.
opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__ANALYSIS:
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary, the fact that being an under trial accused the appellant is in jail since 01.08.2022 and the charge is yet to be framed
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this appeal is allowed subject to a condition that after release on bail, the appellant will not try to make any contact with the prosecutrix in any manner.
opennyai_summary.20_April_2023__decision:
, I am inclined to enlarge him on bail.
It is made clear that if such an act is reported against the appellant, then the respondent/State will be at liberty to move an appropriate application for cancellation of bail granted to the appellant.
It is directed that the appellant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.
It is further directed that the appellant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
